Latin anōmalialbor. English anomaly From Latin anomalia, from Ancient Greek ἀνωμαλία (anōmalía, “irregularity, anomaly”), from ἀνώμαλος (anṓmalos, “irregular, uneven”), negating the meaning of ὁμαλός (homalós, “even”), from ὁμός (homós, “same”).

senses.d: A deviation from a rule or from what is regarded as normal; an outlier.
Something or someone that is strange or unusual.
ex: He is an anomaly among his friends in that he's the only one who's unmarried.

senses.d: Any event or measurement that is out of the ordinary regardless of whether it is exceptional or not.
ex: She disregarded some of the anomalies in the experiment, putting them down to miscalculation.

senses.d: A failure of a classical symmetry due to quantum corrections.

grp.label: something or someone that is strange or unusual
science: any event, big or small, out of the ordinary
astronomy: any of various angular distances

ety.text: Ultimately a borrowing from Ancient Greek ἀνωμαλία (anōmalía).

es:anomalía.gl: anomaly (a deviation from a rule or from what is regarded as normal)

ety.text: Borrowed from Latin anōmalia, from Ancient Greek ἀνωμαλία (anōmalía).
Learned borrowing from Latin anōmalia, from Ancient Greek ἀνωμαλία (anōmalía, “irregularity, anomaly”), from ἀνώμαλος (anṓmalos, “irregular, uneven”), negating the meaning of ὁμαλός (homalós).

Borrowed into English around 1600 from Late Latin anonymus, from Ancient Greek ᾰ̓νώνῠμος (ănṓnŭmos, “without name”), from ᾰ̓ν- (ăn-, “un-”) with ὄνῠμᾰ (ónŭmă), Aeolic and Doric dialectal form of ὄνομᾰ (ónomă, “name”). English equivalent anonym + -ous, its full etymology being an- + -onym + -ous.

senses.d: Lacking a name; not named, for example an animal not assigned to any species .
Without any name acknowledged of a person responsible.
Of unknown name; whose name is withheld

ex: an anonymous office block in a soulless industrial estate

ety.text: Ancient Greek ἀνώνυμος (anṓnumos)bor. Late Latin anōnymuslbor. Portuguese anónimo Learned borrowing from Late Latin anōnymus.
From Middle English another. By surface analysis, an + other.

senses.d: One more further, in addition to the quantity by then; a second or additional one, similar in likeness or in effect.
ex: Yes, I'd like another slice of cake, thanks.
Do you know another way to do this job?
But that is another story and will be told another time.

senses.d: Any or some other, similar in likeness or in effect, instead.
ex: One gold ingot is valued the same as another, but gemstones are valued individually.
But that is another story and will be told another time.

senses.d: An additional one of the same kind.
ex: This napkin fell to the floor, could you please bring me another?
There is one sterling and here is another

senses.d: One that is different from the current one.
ex: I saw one movie, but I think I will see another.
I've thought about moving to another city at one time or another.

senses.d: One of a group of things of the same kind.
ex: His interests keep shifting from one thing to another.

grp.label: one more, in addition to a former number
